content.biomarker_guidance: Trials of biomarkers (particularly BNP and/or NT-proBNP) to guide pharmacotherapy for HFrEF have produced conflicting results. BNP/NT-proBNP are good prognostic markers but current evidence does not support routine measurement of BNP or NT-proBNP to guide titration of therapy.
content.telemonitoring_definition: Telemonitoring (home telemonitoring, HTM) enables remote collection of digital health information (symptoms, weight, heart rate, blood pressure) stored in electronic records to support/adjust patient care and reduce clinic visits and travel costs.
content.telemonitoring_practical_points: HTM systems are diverse (local, regional, national); adherence may be incomplete. Some systems focus on continuous optimization of care (health maintenance approach) rather than anticipating episodic worsening (which generates many false positives). HTM can provide prompt access and support but should integrate with existing healthcare provision.
content.evidence_summary_and_effect_sizes: A 2017 Cochrane review identified 39 relevant HTM trials and found HTM associated with a reduction in all-cause mortality (~20%) and HF hospitalization (~37%). Since then several neutral trials and at least one positive trial have been published, unlikely to overturn the systematic-review findings.
content.wearables_and_novel_sensors: Uncertain whether wearable technologies for monitoring heart rate/rhythm or lung congestion (bio-impedance or radar) add benefits beyond conventional HTM.
content.implanted_device_monitoring: Many implanted therapeutic devices can wirelessly report device status (generator/lead function), arrhythmias, and patient physiology (heart rate, activity, heart sounds, bio-impedance). Monitoring can detect device malfunction earlier than conventional monitoring and may detect arrhythmias such as atrial fibrillation, but evidence that device monitoring reduces HF admissions or mortality is limited.
content.monitoring_only_devices_and_pulmonary_pr: Monitoring-only devices (implantable loop recorders) can be injected subcutaneously to monitor heart rate/rhythm, activity, bio-impedance. Pulmonary-artery pressure monitors can measure pressure remotely; a preliminary trial showed reduction in recurrent HF hospitalization and a larger trial (GUIDE-HF) completed recruitment.
content.overall_conclusion: Telemonitoring and device-based monitoring show promise for supporting HF care and early detection of device issues/arrhythmias, with systematic-review evidence of reduced mortality and hospitalizations for HTM; however, heterogeneity of systems, mixed trial results since 2017, and limited evidence that device monitoring alone reduces admissions or mortality mean careful integration and further evidence are required.
